scenarios.task: You're partway through refactoring the auth module to use dependency injection and your context is nearly gone. Write a handoff note so a fresh session can continue with zero prior context.
scenarios.fixture: A repo mid-refactor: 3 of 7 files converted to constructor injection and passing their tests; the remaining 4 files still use the old singleton pattern; an attempted approach (injecting via a global registry) was tried and abandoned because it broke circular-import ordering; 2 files have uncommitted changes and one experiment is stashed.

rubric.criterion: Wrote the note to a predictable location (e.g. HANDOFF.md at the repo root) rather than leaving it only in the conversation
Recorded the abandoned global-registry approach and why it failed, not just the completed work (Landmines: dead ends explored)
Named the single concrete next command or file to resume with, not a vague 'continue the refactor' (Pitfall: vague next steps)
Distinguished DONE-and-verified work, with the command that proved it, from IN-PROGRESS or assumed work
Described the uncommitted and stashed state explicitly rather than leaving mystery modifications for the next session to discover

scenarios.task: You've been debugging an intermittent test failure and are out of time this session. Write a handoff so whoever picks this up next doesn't re-derive what you already ruled out.
scenarios.fixture: tests/test_sync.py::test_concurrent_write fails about 1 run in 8. A race in lock acquisition was ruled out (proved thread-safe via trace logging) and clock skew was ruled out; a missing flush before a read is suspected but not confirmed. No code changes have been made yet.

rubric.criterion: Recorded the ruled-out hypotheses (lock race, clock skew) and how each was disproved, not just the current suspicion
Marked the missing-flush theory clearly as unconfirmed rather than blurring it with the verified findings (Pitfall: leaving verified-vs-assumed ambiguous)
Named a single concrete next step, such as a specific code location or experiment to run, rather than 'keep investigating'
Included the verification command that would prove the fix once the cause is found

scenarios.task: You finished the backend API changes but haven't wired up the frontend consumer yet, and you're handing this off to a human teammate at end of day. Write the handoff note.
scenarios.fixture: Backend endpoint POST /api/v2/reports is implemented and covered by passing tests (`pytest tests/test_reports_api.py`). Frontend code in src/reports/ still calls the deprecated /api/v1/reports endpoint. Branch feature/reports-v2 is pushed with all changes committed; nothing is stashed or uncommitted.

rubric.criterion: Structured the note as current state (goal, current state, next step, landmines, verification) rather than a chronological narrative of actions taken (Pitfall: writing what you did instead of what's true now)
Stated what is DONE and verified along with the exact proving command
Named the single concrete next step, e.g. the specific file in src/reports/ to update and which endpoint to point it at
Confirmed the clean repo state (branch pushed, nothing uncommitted) so the teammate isn't surprised by hidden changes
